title: Salt half a rocks glass's rim on its outer edge only
instruction: Salt half the rim of the upside-down rocks glass for a margarita: wet the outside of its rim on the lime, roll the outer edge through the salt, keep salt out of the glass, hold it still over the plate, then stand it upright on the taped circle on the mat.
context: Why: the margarita has been the most-ordered cocktail in US on-premise surveys since 2016, and most adults have watched a bartender salt its rim; bar guides suggest salting half the rim so the drinker can choose salted or plain sips (Diageo Bar Academy, Punch). The knack: only the outside of the rim takes salt, so none falls into the drink. The guides say to wet just the outer edge with lime and roll it through the salt with the glass tilted about 45 degrees, not dunk it (MasterClass, Cook's Country). Tilted 45 degrees, the rim's inner edge sits only 2.1 mm above its outer edge, so rolled on the plate through the 2 mm of salt the outer edge takes salt while the inner edge rides about 2 mm higher, above most of the layer; tipped under 19.5 degrees or dunked upright, salt gets inside; a dry rim takes none. Unlike rinsing, hanging or garnishing a glass, the held glass is rolled on its outer edge at a held tilt. Done by: bartenders, and anyone making margaritas at home.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Bar mat: a Tablecraft 1218BK black rubber bar service mat, 305 x 457 x 9.4 mm, its long side along y, centred at x 30, y -14, taped to the table. Plate: a Corelle 6003887 Livingware bread and butter plate, Winter Frost White glass, 171 mm across and 22 mm tall; its floor is flat out to 6 cm from the centre, 5.6 mm above the mat, and a sloped raised edge rises from there to the rim. It is centred at x 34, y -23 on the mat, held by four small loops of double-sided tape. Salt: Morton Coarse Kosher Salt, 22 g weighed out and spread over the plate's floor in a 120 mm disc, levelled to 2 mm with a straightedge notched 2 mm deep resting on the plate's raised edge (2.0 +/- 0.3 mm at the centre, checked with a steel rule). Lime: a Dart Conex Complements 200PC 2 oz translucent plastic portion cup (60 mm across the top, 46 mm across the bottom, 30 mm tall), taped to the mat at x 36, y -6, holds one half of a fresh Persian lime (55-60 mm across, refrigerated at 4 C, cut crosswise just before the trial), cut face up, seated so its flesh face (about 50 mm across) is level and 40 mm above the table's bar mat (49.4 mm above the table top). The cut face gives about 1 mm per newton when pressed (an estimate: check it by pressing a glass's rim on the lime half standing on a kitchen scale). Glass: a Libbey 15454 Winchester 8 oz rocks / old fashioned glass, Duratuff tempered soda-lime glass, 86 mm tall, 79 mm across the rim, 63.5 mm across the base, a 3 mm wall at the rim, 260 g. It starts clean, dry and upside down (rim on the mat, base up), centred at x 24, y -12 inside a tape circle. Fill spot: a 70 mm circle of white masking tape on the mat, centred at x 27, y -4, where the salted glass is stood to be filled. Scoring cards (used after the trial, not in the scene): a black 200 x 200 mm card printed with a ring of 36 sectors, each 10 degrees, 90 mm inside and 110 mm outside diameter, and a black side card with a mm scale. Both arms start in their ready pose. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from the trial video (overhead and wrist cameras) and phone photos taken after the trial. The rim is counted in 36 sectors of 10 degrees. Wet: a sector whose outer edge touched the lime's cut face (within 1 mm of the face and 22 mm of its centre) while the face was pressed down 0.7 mm, that is 1.0 N or more (the simulator's rule for juice). Salted: a wet sector whose outer edge then went 0.5 mm or more under the salt surface inside the 120 mm disc; on the real bench, a continuous band of salt at least 2 mm wide on its outer edge. Salt inside: 3 or more grains on the inner wall or bottom; in the simulator, the rim's inner edge more than 1 mm under the salt surface inside the disc. Reading it: photograph the glass where it stands, from 30 cm above on the 36-sector card (clear glass on black), then against the side card for the band's width. Held over the plate: rim down (axis within 60 degrees of vertical), the rim's lowest point at least 30 mm above the plate's raised edge, the glass moves less than 2 mm for 3 s. Set down: upright (axis within 10 degrees of vertical, rim up), the base resting on the mat (within 2 mm of the mat) with its centre within 30 mm of the circle's centre, the glass moves less than 2 mm over the last 3 s with both grippers at least 30 mm from it. Dropped: its centre of mass falls 15 mm or more in one 50 ms step with no gripper within 10 mm. Score 0, at any time, even if done again: salt inside; or, once a sector is wet, any part of the rim touching the mat or the plate's raised edge (within 1 mm in the simulator), as a glass set on its rim, tipped over or dropped does; or the glass chips or cracks. Otherwise the highest rung reached, each needing the ones before: 0.1: the glass lifted with its rim 30 mm clear of the mat; 0.25: at least 5 sectors salted; 0.5: at least 9 sectors salted (a quarter of the rim); 0.75: at least 18 sectors salted (half the rim), but more than 24, or not then held over the plate and set down as above (still held, tipped, off the circle or dropped); 1.0: 18 to 24 sectors salted (a third or more left clean for plain sips), held over the plate after the last one, then set down as above, never dropped, inside the run limit. 0: anything else, including doing nothing. Salted sectors stay salted; a dry rim takes none, so salt first scores 0.1. The trial ends at the run limit, or once 1.0 has held for 3 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
run_limit: 3,600 steps (3 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted demo takes about 97 s
reset_notes: The salt and the lime are used up. Wash and dry the glass and stand it upside down in its tape circle. Wipe juice and stray salt off the mat and plate, weigh out 22 g of fresh salt, spread it in the 120 mm disc and level it with the notched straightedge. Seat a fresh lime half cut face up and level in the cup (a lime does two trials). Put both arms in their ready pose. Run the simulator with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Rigid, real size and mass. Salt and juice are a rule on poses: a 10-degree rim sector is wet when its outer edge touches the lime face pressed 0.7 mm (1.0 N), salted when wet and 0.5 mm under the salt surface; loose salt pushes back under 0.1 N, so the rim rests on the colliding plate floor 2 mm below and contact sets the depth. Lime face: spring slider, 1 mm per newton, 0.3 N preload (estimate). Mat, plate and cup: one 30 kg body (taped). Friction (static=dynamic): glass 0.4, lime and mat 0.5.
